details: Following President Trump's indications of a potential US-Iran agreement and the cancellation of planned military actions, Asian equity markets saw gains, oil prices declined, and risk assets, including Bitcoin, rallied approximately 5% to reach near $77,000. Bitcoin experienced intraday price swings of 4-7% in response to these geopolitical developments.
title: US-Iran De-escalation Boosts Markets and Bitcoin

details: The European Central Bank (ECB) increased its key interest rates by 25 basis points on June 11, marking its first hike since 2023. This action indicates a shift towards tighter monetary conditions within the eurozone, which could potentially curb cryptocurrency market growth and intensify competition for decentralized finance (DeFi) platforms.
title: ECB Rate Hike Signals Tighter Monetary Conditions

details: Jack Mallers suggested that Bitcoin's recent price drop is a reflection of a global liquidity crisis, rather than weak crypto sentiment. He considers Bitcoin the "most honest indicator" of the current global economic situation, implying that its price reacts to a real shortage of cash in the system, and that global liquidity conditions are more crucial for predicting its near-term trajectory than on-chain metrics.
title: Mallers: Bitcoin Price Reflects Global Liquidity Crisis

details: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) reports a surge in stablecoin adoption in emerging markets, driven by factors such as foreign exchange volatility, inflation, weak institutional frameworks, and poor policy credibility. While primarily originating in advanced economies, stablecoins' macro-financial impact disproportionately affects emerging markets, potentially reducing cross-border payment costs and fostering financial inclusion.
title: Stablecoin Adoption Surges in Emerging Markets
